summary: Provision minimized derivative log sample for Privacy Engineering research into billing classification regression
description:
Issue summary: Request from Privacy Engineering to provision a small, derivative-only sample of production inference logs to reproduce a billing-classification regression detected in EU billing data.

Impact: Low production risk if handled correctly; necessary for reproducing and fixing a regression affecting invoicing for a handful of customers in eu-west. No PII should be included in provided artifacts.

Background: Engineering observed a mismatch between per-customer billed token counts and tokenization expectations for long-chat sessions. Privacy Eng needs a representative signal from real traces to validate tokenizer-edge conditions. Customer-identifying fields must not be present; we will provide derivative artifacts (statistical counts, tokenized snippets with hashed session IDs, and redaction markers) rather than raw plaintext.

Requested deliverable: A timeboxed (48h) bundle containing up to 2,000 anonymized request/response pairs converted into derivative artifacts: token counts, tokenized-safe-snippets (first 50 tokens only), hashed session id, region tag, model-version, and a flag if KV-cache prefixing occurred. Raw request text or raw customer payload must not be included.

Data scope and filters: timeframe 2026-02-20 to 2026-02-27; region eu-west only; models: rdx-3b, rdx-3b-quant; only sessions where billed_token_count deviates >20% from computed_token_count.

Retention and handling: Artifacts will be hosted in a short-lived S3 bucket with server-side KMS encryption and a bucket policy restricting access to the approved list. Data TTL: 7 days, after which bucket lifecycle will permanently delete objects and KMS keys will be scheduled for rotation. No download outside company VPN; all access through ephemeral credentials logged.

Access controls and reviewers: Access will be limited to Privacy Engineering (2 named engineers), one member of Billing Ops, and the compliance reviewer (Legal). Approvers required: Head of Privacy (Maya Singh) and Security Manager (Omar Ruiz).

Approval required: This ticket requests approval for the data extraction and to proceed with scripted redaction and derivation steps. Please respond with explicit approval or requested constraints. If approved, Engineering will schedule the extract in the next 48h maintenance window.

Timeline: Approval within 48h requested; extraction to occur in a scheduled 2-hour window; artifacts available for 7 days.

Attachments: Link to reproducible test harness and tokenizer check scripts in internal repo.

resolution: Provisioned a 48-hour, derivative-only artifact bundle in s3://rbw-derivative-eu-west/INT-995001/ with KMS encryption. Access granted to approved list for 7 days. After validation, Privacy Eng confirmed the artifacts were sufficient to reproduce tokenizer edge case; Billing discrepancy root-cause assigned to Tokenization Team (ENG-2248).
